claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your situation, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you a few more questions about Alex to determine eligibility.

Since Alex is 19, Child Benefit can continue beyond age 16 if the young person is in approved education or training (up until they turn 20). 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in full-time non-advanced education, or on an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. He's doing something, but I don't know all the details about whether it counts as approved or what type it is exactly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it can be unclear what counts as approved education or training. Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Can you tell me what Alex is doing during the day?** For example, is he:
- Attending college or sixth form?
- At university?
- On an apprenticeship?
- In some kind of training program?
- Working?
- Or something else?

Even general information about what he's doing would be helpful.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's just at home with me most of the time. He's not really doing much of anything at the moment - not working or studying or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to make sure I have the complete picture:

1. **Where do you live - are you living in the UK?**

2. **Have you been receiving Child Benefit for Alex previously, or is this a new claim you're considering?**

Let me start with the first question - do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And my second question:

**Have you been receiving Child Benefit for Alex previously, or is this a new claim you're considering?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to claim it - that's why I'm asking whether I'm eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have enough information now to assess Alex's eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 19 years old
- He lives at home with you in the UK
- He is not currently in education, training, or work
- You are considering making a claim for Child Benefit

Unfortunately, this means Alex would not be eligible for Child Benefit. Here's why:

Child Benefit normally stops when a child turns 16. It can continue if the young person is under 20 **and** stays in approved education or training. Since Alex is 19 and is not in any education or training, he does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit.

If Alex's circumstances were to change - for example, if he starts approved education or training - you could potentially claim then, as long as he's still under 20.

Let me formally record this assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry that the outcome isn't what you were hoping for. If Alex does decide to start education or training in the future while he's still under 20, you may want to look into claiming Child Benefit at that point. Is there anything else I can help clarify?
